findings.fingerprint_key: {"defect_class":"missing-pre-migration-real-host-stop-gate","lens":"integration + coverage","locations":["tasks.json phases 0–2 (0.1.1, 0.1.2, 1.2.3) vs 2.1.2/4.2.3/5.1.3/6.2.2; execute.md wave plan"],"severity":"Blocker"}

locations: tasks.json phases 0–2 (0.1.1, 0.1.2, 1.2.3) vs 2.1.2/4.2.3/5.1.3/6.2.2; execute.md Wave Plan

source_evidence.finding: Plan §2.5 ("On failure, stop before migration") and Phase 1 Succeeds-when (c)/(d) require a real Codex run proving one prose-heavy and one code-heavy accepted fixture arrive inline, with a dated evidence artifact, BEFORE migration or user-data changes. No task executes this: 0.1.1 only *documents* commands/observations, 0.1.2 is RED tests, 1.2.3's ACs only require the harness to *emit* commands/manifest. Real-host execution first happens at 6.2.2 (wave 9) — after the migration engine (2.1.2, wave 3) is wired to user data via SessionStart (4.2.3, wave 5) and install/update (5.1.3, wave 6). Plan Phase 1 bullet "Run a minimal real Claude/Codex hook probe" maps to no task. execute.md's wave-0 rationale and slicing rule ("Preserve … the Phase 0 payload stop gate") describe a gate the graph does not contain.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Insert Verification subtask **1.2.4 "Execute Phase-1 real-host payload probe"** (predecessor 1.2.3; consumed_by 2.1.1). ACs: (observable) one accepted prose and one accepted code fixture arrive inline in a real Codex run per §2.5 with no preview/saved-file/truncation/fallback notice; (state) dated `docs/tasks/main/knowledge-surfacing/verification/host-payload-YYYY-MM-DD.md` saved; (state) on any fallback, execution stops before Phase 2 and measured estimator values + observed behavior are appended to `task_context.md`. Gate 2.1 on it and insert a wave between wave-2 and wave-3 in execute.md. Note the sub-dependency: the probe must install the runtime into the Codex fixture, so give 1.2.4 a minimal copy path independent of the full recursive translator (or pull a minimal nested-sync step forward from 6.1.2). Update REQ-017 tasks to include the new gate.

source_evidence.finding: 3.1.3 produces `spectre knowledge search|register|migrate` routing and its AC requires `src/main.test.js` to pass for **all three** subcommands — but `registerKnowledge` lands in 2.2.2 (wave 4, after 3.1) and `migrateLegacyKnowledge` in 2.1.2 (wave 3, parallel, unordered). Also asymmetric: 2.2.2 `consumed_by` lists 3.1, but parent 2.2 `unblocks` ("3.2, 4.2, 5.1") omits 3.1.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Preferred: split 3.1.3 into search-only routing (stays wave 3) and a new "wire register/migrate routing" subtask ordered after 2.2.2 (under 5.1 or a new parent). Alternative: add 2.2 to 3.1's predecessor, add 3.1 to 2.2's unblocks, move 3.1 to wave 5 and re-cascade. Either way, reconcile 2.2.2 consumed_by with the parent graph.

source_evidence.finding: 4.2.3's AC "spectre-apply removed only after all runtime, manifest, and test references are gone" is unsatisfiable at wave 5. Verified references that outlive it: `plugins/spectre/skills/spectre-recall/SKILL.md` (rewritten by *parallel* 3.2.2 — no edge, despite 3.2.2 consumed_by listing 4.2); `src/lib/knowledge.js:83,160` reads `spectre-apply/SKILL.md` at install time and `src/install.test.js:62` asserts it (cut over only in 5.1.x, wave 6); `.claude/skills/verify-spectre/references/expected-skills.txt:8` lists `spectre-apply` and no task updates it, yet 6.2.1 requires the verify-spectre gates to pass. Deleting at wave 5 breaks install runtime and two gates mid-plan.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add 3.2 to 4.2's predecessor (makes 3.2.2→4.2 symmetric). Move the *file deletion* of `spectre-apply/SKILL.md` into a new subtask ordered after 5.1.2 (e.g. under 5.2 or as 6.1.0) whose ACs include purging the verify-spectre expected-skills references (`.claude` and `.agents` copies) and regenerating the mirror. Leave 4.2.3 removing runtime/manifest wiring only; update 6.1.1's "obsolete apply removal" fixture context.

source_evidence.finding: 3.2.2 deletes `spectre-learn/references/recall-template.md` at wave 5, but npm-side readers survive until wave 6: `src/lib/knowledge.js:74-76` (`recallTemplatePath` used by `ensureKnowledgeFiles`) and `src/install.test.js:77`. The precondition in 3.2.1's own AC ("after all generation references are removed") cannot hold; deletion at wave 5 breaks install/update and install tests until 5.1 lands.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Move the physical template deletion into 5.1.2 (or a post-5.1.2 subtask with predecessor 5.1.2); 3.2.2 drops only the skill's references. Update 3.2.1 AC3 to require deletion after the `src/lib/knowledge.js` references are gone, and update 3.2.2's produces text.

source_evidence.finding: 3.2.1 produces "failing static and workflow assertions" for skill contracts, but no skill-contract test harness exists anywhere in the repo (verified), plan §13 names no such test file, and "workflow assertions" against LLM-executed prose skills are not machine-falsifiable. The implementer must invent both the mechanism and the location — guaranteed drift.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: In 3.2.1 produces, name `plugins/spectre/hooks/scripts/test_skill-contracts.mjs` (matches the `npm test` glob) and define the assertions as concrete text checks: learn/recall SKILL.md must NOT contain `.claude/skills` write paths, `registry.toon`, `{{REGISTRY}}`, or `recall-template.md` references; MUST contain `spectre knowledge search`, the dual size-gate retry loop, and the `~/.spectre/projects` store path; `references/recall-template.md` must not exist (timing per finding 4). Drop or redefine "workflow assertions" as these static checks.

source_evidence.finding: Plan Phase 4 Succeeds-when ends "…and the §2.5 real-host protocol records equivalent inline behavior within host limits." No 4.x task carries a real-host criterion; the clause is silently deferred to 6.2.2 (wave 9), so installer cutover (5.x) is built on unverified real hook behavior and the phase gate cannot be satisfied by the tasks in its phase.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add an observable AC to 4.2.2 or a Verification subtask 4.2.4: "The §2.5 protocol, run against the completed resolver, records equivalent inline primary content and notice on real Claude and Codex within host limits, appended to the dated evidence artifact." Gate 5.1 on it.

source_evidence.finding: 3.1.2 claims matcher parent 4.1 as a consumer, but 3.1 and 4.1 run in parallel in wave 3 with no edge. Plan separates search ranking from the trigger matcher, and 4.1's secondary entries embed only a textual CLI search hint — the edge is either false or a missing ordering.

source_evidence.finding: Nested `knowledge/*.mjs` modules land at wave 1 but recursive translation lands at wave 8. Verified: `listRuntimeMjsFiles` is flat, so `npm run sync-codex -- --check` stays green while the Codex mirror silently lacks the runtime, and from wave 5 the generated hooks carry an unrewritten `--host claude`. CLAUDE.md's sync-after-every-change workflow gives false confidence in waves 1–7.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Either move 6.1.1+6.1.2 earlier (they depend only on the `knowledge/` directory contract), or add an explicit note to 1.1.2, 4.2.2, and 5.1.3: "Generated `plugins/spectre-codex` is known-incomplete until 6.1.2; sync --check green does not imply mirror completeness."

source_evidence.finding: Plan §5 "Atomic registration" includes "concurrent writers yield one complete record and a rebuildable index" — no criterion asserts that end state (lock semantics and injected-failure atomicity are covered; the two-writer outcome is not).
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add test AC to 2.2.2: "Two concurrent registration attempts against one store serialize: exactly one complete committed record and a valid rebuildable index; the losing writer returns a lock-timeout error, not a partial write."

source_evidence.finding: RED gap: 1.1.2's "injected failure before rename leaves prior canonical JSON bytes unchanged" has no corresponding fixture demanded of 1.1.1 (identity/collision/lock only), so the Build criterion can be greened without a failing test ever existing.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add test AC to 1.1.1: "A fixture injects a failure between temp-file write and rename in `test_knowledge-store.mjs` and asserts prior `project.json`/`index.json` bytes are unchanged."

source_evidence.finding: RED gap: 2.2.2 AC1 includes "lock timeout" among passing registration cases, but 2.2.1 requires only "atomic retries" — no lock-timeout error-path test is demanded of the RED task.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add to 2.2.1: "A held store lock makes registration return a lock-timeout error without partial writes (RED until implemented)."

source_evidence.finding: "Known unsafe fixtures are rejected" is undefined at execution time — unsafety is only knowable after a real host run shows fallback, which (finding 1) has no owning task before 1.2.3 is judged done.
source_evidence.suggested_edit: Define in 1.2.3: unsafe = framed output exceeding 9,000 chars (Claude) or the recorded Codex estimator budget constant; constants + measured rationale live in the payload module and are asserted by tests. Pair with new 1.2.4 (finding 1) to validate the constants against reality.

source_evidence.suggested_edit: Add state AC to 1.2.3: "Each fixture class's measured accepted boundary is a named constant with a rationale comment; tests reference the constants, not literals."

source_evidence.finding: "Isolated Git, linked-worktree, and non-Git integration fixtures pass migration, match, search, install, doctor, and uninstall checks" — no prior task produces a composite fixture suite of that shape, so a Verification-type task would have to author tests, i.e. unpaired mid-task scope invention at the final gate.

source_evidence.finding: Oversized multi-concern subtasks (est. 400–550 LOC each): 1.1.2 = identity resolution + collision expansion + `withStoreLock`/stale recovery + atomic writes + `src/lib/paths.js` adapter; 2.1.2 = 8-code classification + staging + atomic commit + cleanup ordering + crash-resume + contention + report; 5.1.3 = config filtering + install/update migration integration. (4.2.3 is also oversized; its split is part of finding 3.)
